Voat is currently gamified to encourage consumption and participation which in general is a good thing, but it can be too much of a good thing for some of us who struggle to stop. It would me nice if the gamification was modified to encourage users to healthily limit their consumption and participation on voat.

I personally sometimes struggle to stop voating on /v/all content. Sure, sometimes I get bored and manage to stop without difficulty, but other times it serves as an unhealthy escape from my responsibilitIes. I think there are many ways the gamification could be modified so I don't want this suggestion to hinge on the viability of any particular way of addressing the issue, but I also feel like I should provide at least some concrete idea of how it might could be done.

One idea would be to have a preference which if enabled would say something like "Thanks for helping make Voat great! Now get off the Internet and don't come back until tomorrow!" And you could perhaps start with just inline warnings, but at some later point start redirecting pretty much all HTTP requests to a page with nothing but that message. As far as measuring what's too much, you could base it on lots of different things such as number of viewed pages, links, or comments, the number of up or down voats, the number of submitted links or comments, the number of words submitted, or the amount of time spent active on the site.

Another idea is to perhaps use some new or existing point system to encourage healthy usage.
Too Much of a Goat Thing

Asking developers to work on something that decreases participation is not realistic.

Take control of it yourself. http://alternativeto.net/software/cold-turkey/

If the site received ad based revenue I'd agree, but since it doesn't, I might go so far as to speculate that the developers might possibly maybe have the users' best interests at heart. Shocking, I know!

Concerning taking control of myself, I addressed that in my other reply.

Gaining the ability to downvoat is the initial objective, and by the time you've achieved that, you've become accustomed to participation and they've got ya hooked on validating and invalidating thoughts and ideas that you agree with, moving them up and down, influencing people and being influenced; essentially winning or losing the hearts and minds of humanity.

Voat also provides a never ending supply of links and discussion that is curated for popularity and freshness, the consumption of which can, like the best of games, be quite behaviorally addictive, especially when combined with responsive discussion feedback and the rest of the gamification mentioned above.

Getting hooked on fresh content and validating or invalidating others' ideas is a personality trait that you need to find ways to address.

Voat, like all internet discussion sites, wants fresh content because that's what the users (like you and I) want. There is no evil mastermind scheming to get us addicted to voat.

Others have mentioned timers and apps to help control internet usage, I suggest you use them rather than attempting to hamstring voat as a discussion platform. While voat could implement features to assist users with low willpower, those users could simply turn off the limiting features, bringing us back to the root problem.

I think that doing it at the site level adds value to the site. Some random high risk application does not add value to the site. And in any case, I don't want some overly intrusive security nightmare of an application telling me I've spent too much time on the Internet. I don't have an issue with the rest of the Internet. The rest of the Internet is lame in comparison to Voat. What I do want is for my beloved Voat to tell me when I have achieved a maximum healthy level of participation for the day. Not only can it help me to stop at a well defined stopping point, which Voat currently lacks, it may also occasionally encourage me to participate more on days that I might have otherwise slacked from my voating responsibilities.

Not being able to downvoat initially is one of the best features of voat, yet it's a restriction. It may have been intended only as a restriction and nothing more, but it is more. My experience with that restriction directly added value to my personal user experience on Voat. I didn't care that some links and comments had less downvoats; I simply loved being pushed and prodded to participate in discussions by the fun slight frustration of not being able to downvoat.

I appreciate your feedback and thanks for the suggestions, but I stand by my idea. :-)
